answer: In an agent economy, a work-plus-stake proof makes identity costly: each new agent earns standing only by completing verified tasks that are unique to a real context, then locks a rising walnut-sized collateral behind its reputation. A crowd of fake agents must therefore pay real stake per identity and keep producing distinct, attestable outputs, so a gale of signups cannot blow cheap accounts into influence. The ledger acts as an atlas of earned history, not claims, and cost scales linearly for each fake peer.
